series.series_status: Brewers lead the series 1-0 after a 3-2 win in Game 1 on Friday. Game 2 is Saturday at 7:00 PM at American Family Field.
series.format: Best of seven. Brewers (103-59, best record in MLB) have home field: Games 1, 2, 6*, 7* in Milwaukee; Games 3, 4, 5* at Tropicana Field, St. Petersburg (* if necessary).
series.milwaukee_angle: The Brewers are in the World Series, and they won Game 1 on Friday, 3-2. Game 2 is Saturday night in Milwaukee, the same night as the second Riverside show. It is the Brewers' first World Series since 1982 and the second in franchise history. They went a franchise-record 103-59, beat the Padres in the NLDS and swept the Dodgers in the NLCS. Neither team has ever won a World Series, so a first-time champion is guaranteed. Downtown will be blue and gold: free outdoor watch parties in the Deer District, a two-day block party in the Third Ward, bars running Brewers specials. Resale get-in was about $2,700-$2,900 as of Oct 20, so the ballpark is out, but being downtown this weekend is being inside the biggest Milwaukee sports moment in 44 years.
storylines: The Brewers set a franchise record with 103 wins and led MLB in wins for the second straight year.
Milwaukee swept the Dodgers in the NLCS to get here. Tampa Bay swept the Yankees in the ALDS and beat Cleveland in six in the ALCS.
The Brewers took 2 of 3 from the Rays in their only regular-season series (Mar 30-Apr 1).
The last Brewers World Series was 1982, 'Harvey's Wallbangers,' lost to the Cardinals in 7. Expect 1982 nostalgia everywhere.
series.tv: FOX (free over the air) and FOX Deportes
series.home_game_ticket_note: Games 1 and 2 at American Family Field are the hottest tickets in Milwaukee history. Resale get-in was estimated at $2,920 (Game 1) and $2,689 (Game 2) as of Oct 20. Both games overlap the Widespread Panic shows, so this is a watch-party weekend, not a ballpark weekend.

games.note: Christian Yelich tripled in a run in his first World Series at-bat, and Trevor Megill struck out Jonny DeLuca with the tying run on third to end it.

7:00 PM first pitch against a ~7:30 PM set 1. Saturday has the fuller daytime menu: the Third Ward block party noon-11 PM with FOX One's retro 'Relive Live' pop-up (noon-4 PM) and Foul Territory live (5-7 PM) at Catalano Square, the Deer Garden big screen in the Deer District, and 90s2K Cafe's '1982 Retro Watch Party' (doors 5 PM, 82-cent taps 6-7 PM). First pitch somewhere close to the Riverside, then the show, then the score at set break. If the Brewers win and go up 2-0 heading to Tampa, downtown will be a party until bar close (2:30 AM).

No game Sunday, the travel day between Milwaukee and Tampa Bay. The one night of the stay with zero baseball conflict. Sports bars will have the Packers instead (Tom's Watch Bar lists a Packers watch party at 3:25 PM).

After the ~3 PM flight, so Game 3 is a watch-from-home game. The Brewers are opening American Family Field as a $15 watch party for Games 3 and 4 (gates 5 PM), and those tickets sold out in about 20 minutes on Oct 22.

if_series_ends_early: Hi Baby, it cannot. A best-of-seven cannot end before Game 4 on Tuesday Oct 27, so Game 2 on Saturday will be played while you are in town, and the series will still be alive when you fly out Monday afternoon. The only weather risk is a postponement, and American Family Field has a retractable roof, so rain or cold will not postpone Games 1 or 2. If a game is somehow rescheduled, check mlb.com/brewers.

getting_around.deer_district: About a half-mile walk north of the Riverside (10-12 minutes): west over the river on Wisconsin Ave, then north on N Vel R. Phillips Ave (Old World Third St / MLK Dr) to Fiserv Forum. The Hop streetcar does not serve the Deer District.
getting_around.third_ward: About a 12-15 minute walk south on Broadway, or ride The Hop (free): board at the Wisconsin Ave stop a block east of the river, take the L Line or M Line to the Historic Third Ward stop, then walk a couple blocks south on Broadway to Catalano Square. Menomonee St will be closed to cars between Broadway and Milwaukee St for the block party.
getting_around.american_family_field: Only relevant with a game ticket. MCTS CONNECT 1 bus rapid transit runs straight down Wisconsin Ave from in front of the Riverside to Wisconsin Ave & 44th St, a walk from the ballpark. Rideshare works too, with surge pricing and lot congestion on World Series nights. Several downtown bars (Who's on Third, O'Lydia's) run their own game-day shuttles.

watch_spots.name: The Deer Garden at Deer District
watch_spots.address: 1134 N Vel R. Phillips Ave, Milwaukee, WI 53203
watch_spots.blurb: The city's official free outdoor watch party: a big screen in the Deer Garden plaza outside Fiserv Forum, ringed by bars and restaurants running Brewers promotions. This is where Milwaukee goes to lose its mind together.
watch_spots.tv_setup: Large outdoor screen presented by Michelob ULTRA; surrounding bars (Tom's Watch Bar, The Mecca, Good City, etc.) have screens with sound indoors.
watch_spots.hours_this_weekend: Plaza is open all day; Brewers first pitch 7 PM. The Game 2 watch party is listed by WTMJ; the Deer District has not posted its own Saturday schedule. Dress warm; late October nights in Milwaukee run 35-45 F.

watch_spots.name: Tom's Watch Bar
watch_spots.address: 1134 N Vel R. Phillips Ave, Milwaukee, WI 53203
watch_spots.blurb: The most screens in the city, all with the sound up, in a 360-degree stadium-seating room on the Deer District plaza. They have committed to every Brewers postseason game, take reservations for playoff tables (it fills), and the food runs a notch above wings-and-fries. I have not sat in it. Reviewers who have say it is the ballpark without the $2,900 ticket.
watch_spots.tv_setup: More than 100 screens with sound up, oversized 'stadium screens' (reviewers mention a 45-foot jumbotron on the mezzanine), 360-degree viewing, indoor and outdoor seating.
watch_spots.hours_this_weekend: Fri 11:00 AM-12:00 AM; Sat 10:00 AM-12:00 AM; Sun 11:00 AM-12:00 AM; Mon 4:00 PM-12:00 AM. UFC watch Sat 1 PM, Packers watch Sun 3:25 PM.

watch_spots.name: Major Goolsby's
watch_spots.blurb: Milwaukee's old-school sports bar, two blocks from the Riverside, walls covered in signed memorabilia and TVs everywhere. $10 pitchers during every World Series game, giant pretzels, wings, burgers. The closest place to catch first pitch and still make the opening notes of set 1.
watch_spots.tv_setup: TVs throughout the bar and dining room; game audio on for Brewers games (classic sports-bar setup, no single mega-screen).
watch_spots.hours_this_weekend: Fri 11:00 AM-11:00 PM; Sat 11:00 AM-11:00 PM; Sun 11:00 AM-9:00 PM; Mon 4:00-9:00 PM. $10 beer pitchers during every World Series game.

watch_spots.name: Third Ward World Series Block Party (Catalano Square)
watch_spots.blurb: A free street party in the prettiest neighborhood downtown: Menomonee St closed to cars, giant video screens in Catalano Square, food trucks, Brewers-themed cocktails from the Third Ward Beer Garden, and a live taping of the Foul Territory podcast (Corey Knebel, Kevin Pillar, Alanna Rizzo) 5-7 PM. FOX One's 'Relive Live' pop-up is a mock 1980s living room full of Brewers memorabilia and bobbleheads, noon-4 PM.
watch_spots.tv_setup: Giant outdoor video screens in Catalano Square with game audio; the beer garden bar also has TVs.
watch_spots.hours_this_weekend: Sat Oct 24, noon-11:00 PM. Foul Territory live 5-7 PM; FOX One pop-up noon-4 PM; Bill Michaels Show live 10 AM-2 PM. Closed Sunday/Monday.
watch_spots.cost: Free admission; pay for drinks and food
watch_spots.host: Third Ward Beer Garden and the Historic Third Ward Association, with FOX One

watch_spots.name: Cafe Benelux
watch_spots.blurb: Lowlands Group's Belgian-style grand cafe with a rooftop patio in the heart of the Third Ward, two blocks from the block party. Official watch parties with buy-one-get-one Lowlands Brewing Collaborative beers from 5 PM, and they have promised to stay open until the final out. Frites and mussels instead of wings. This one is on reputation, and the reputation is sit-down and grown-up.
watch_spots.tv_setup: TVs throughout the bar and dining rooms; game on for Brewers watch parties.
watch_spots.hours_this_weekend: Fri 7:00 AM-12:00 AM; Sat 7:00 AM-12:00 AM; Sun 7:00 AM-11:00 PM; Mon 7:00 AM-11:00 PM. BOGO Lowlands beers from 5 PM on game days; open until the game ends.

watch_spots.name: 90s2K Cafe
watch_spots.address: 1103 N Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Dr, Milwaukee, WI 53203
watch_spots.blurb: A nostalgia bar (90s and 2000s decor, DJs, big dance floor) a block from the Deer District, throwing a '1982 Retro Watch Party' Saturday for the last time the Brewers were in the World Series. Doors 5 PM, 82-cent taps from 6-7 PM, Brewers gear required for the specials. Loud and young, and a Panic fan would enjoy the pregame.
watch_spots.tv_setup: Multiple TVs (normally playing 90s movies) switched to the game for the watch party.
watch_spots.hours_this_weekend: Watch party Sat Oct 24: doors 5:00 PM, 82-cent taps 6:00-7:00 PM, open until 2:30 AM. Posted regular hours: Sat 4 PM-2:30 AM, Sun 4 PM-2 AM, Mon closed.
watch_spots.cost: No cover listed; Brewers gear required for specials

watch_spots.name: Who's on Third
watch_spots.address: 1007 N Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Dr (Old World Third St), Milwaukee, WI 53203
watch_spots.blurb: The Brewers bar downtown: wings, brats, an outdoor patio, and a game-day shuttle to American Family Field that reviewers come back for on consecutive game days. Four blocks from the Riverside on the walk toward the Deer District. Open until 2:30 AM Friday and Saturday, so it works as a post-show stop for highlights and the mood. Never been inside, but a Brewers bar on a World Series night does not need my review.
watch_spots.tv_setup: Sports-bar TV wall throughout; Brewers games are the house religion.
watch_spots.hours_this_weekend: Fri 11:00 AM-2:30 AM; Sat 11:00 AM-2:30 AM; Sun 11:00 AM-2:00 AM; Mon 11:00 AM-2:00 AM (Google listing). No World Series-specific promo confirmed.

watch_spots.name: Central Waters Brewing Co. Milwaukee Taproom
watch_spots.blurb: A craft brewery taproom inside a converted 1880s church in the old Pabst brewery district, about a 15-minute walk west of the Deer District. The game goes on a projector with audio through the whole bar. World Series specials are $1 off full pours, $4 tallboys of Grand Slam Lager, and 8 bone-in wings with fries for $14, and Trouble Makers Cocina serves Mexican food on site. The calmest option of the watch spots, and the best beer.
watch_spots.tv_setup: Projector screen with game audio throughout the taproom.
watch_spots.hours_this_weekend: Fri 11:00 AM-10:00 PM; Sat 11:00 AM-10:00 PM; Sun 11:00 AM-7:00 PM; Mon 3:00-9:00 PM (posted). Specials run all day on World Series game days; unconfirmed whether they stay open past 10 PM to the final out.
